newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes lower, downtrend could resume.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes lower, downtrend could resume.

text.p: The gold price could take a fresh shot at getting over $380.00 per ounce on Thursday but that would not necessarily change the market's overriding bearish trend, dealers said.
"It is not finished with the $380 yet, but if the resistance is still in there at $380-$381.50, we may see gold moving lower later," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $379.50 per ounce compared with $380.30 on Wednesday afternoon and a close of $380.35/$380.85.
Europe's gains Wednesday, which took gold off 18-month lows, brought little follow-through in New York and the Far East.
"We saw some short covering and partial profit taking yesterday but there were no aggressive signs of trying to take it higher," one dealer said.
The shorts established at and below $383 made some money yesterday but were likely to re-establish their short positions unless the market unexpectedly broke higher.
All through the downtrend from $383 to the recent floor at around $377, neither Comex nor the spot market had seen a day of really heavy selling, dealers said.
"We could see that if it loses $380.00 this time," a dealer said.
A cranking up of the relatively light sales programme could take the $377-$378 floor out of consideration and introduce thoughts of $375, $370 and below, dealers and analysts said.
Physical interest remained very light and was unlikely to re-emerge until there was some assurance that gold had established a base.
Even then it would do no more than underpin. "We will not see this turned round by physical buying," a dealer said.
A range of $378.00-$380.25 was forecast for today.
U.S. jobs data were due on Friday, with payrolls forecast to rise 166,000 against a 250,000 rise in August.
Unemployment was forecast at 5.2 percent for September against 5.1 percent in August.
Dealers said there was very little interest in the rest of the precious metals which were barely changed from Wednesday.
Silver was indicated at an unchanged $4.92/$4.94 and was being treated with caution after making little inroad on its oversold indicators.
Platinum was steady and quiet at $383.75/$384.75, 50 cents off the close and holding barely a $4.00 premium over gold.
